C45222.observed: What was checked: what a part's card in the search list tells you about where that part is kept. What happened: for a part held in four bins the card reads "Inventory Qty: 18 EA" - the total across every bin - and then three bin chips, each with its own count: General Storage 8, A1A 5, A1B 3. The fourth bin is not listed separately; instead the card ends with a "+ 1" chip standing for the one bin not shown. So the card gives the whole picture at a glance and stays a sensible width no matter how many bins a part is spread across.
C45222.not_observed: The third part of this case - that a part in no bins shows "Not stocked" in warning styling - is raised separately as a question: a catalogue part's card says "Catalog" instead, and that may not be the same state the case means.

C45227.observed: What was checked: whether you can overrule the bin the system picked for you. What happened: the system had put the whole quantity on the default bin, General Storage. Opening the chip and choosing A1A instead moved it: the chip immediately read "Pulled from A1A". The whole quantity went across - it was not divided between the two - and the choice then stuck, which is what marks it as one you made deliberately rather than one the system worked out.

C45231.observed: What was checked: whether the system re-thinks the bin when you change the quantity, and whether it respects a bin you chose yourself. What happened, both ways round. Where the bin had been worked out automatically, changing the quantity re-ran the calculation each time and the warning picked up the new number. Where the bin had been chosen by hand - A1A rather than the default - changing the quantity from 3 to 4 kept A1A: it was not quietly moved back to the default. So a deliberate choice is honoured and an automatic one stays current.

C45226.observed: What was checked: what the bin picker offers once a part is held in several bins. What happened: opening the "Pulled from" chip listed every bin the part is in, in catalogue order, each with its stock on hand - General Storage 8, A1A 5, A1B 3, A1C 2. A tick marks the bin currently chosen and a "Default" badge marks the default bin. A1C, which holds fewer than the quantity being asked for, is printed in orange while the bins that can cover it are printed in the ordinary dark text - so a bin that cannot fill the request stands out before you pick it. The list ends with "Split across bins…".
